title: Grateful Dead Live at Gaelic Park on 1971-08-26

ai_review.summary: Good audience tape captures a high‑energy Bronx show with smoking Bertha, St. Stephen, Good Lovin' and an unforgettable Mister Charlie.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience‑sourced tape that, despite occasional cable hum, channel imbalance and drop‑outs, delivers a clear picture of one of the most beloved 1971 Bronx concerts.  The band was on fire – Jerry’s vocals soar, Phil “bombs” on bass, Mickey sits out while Bill drives the beat, and the setlist rolls through Bertha, St. Stephen, Good Lovin’, Hard to Handle and a legendary Mister Charlie.  Overall the performance is remembered as high‑energy and iconic, and listeners forgive the modest technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating across ~30 reviews is 4.1; most comments praise the performance and only note moderate recording issues, yielding a strong combined show‑plus‑recording score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tape‑derived audience mix with occasional cable hum/static, left/right channel imbalance on early discs, and sporadic dropouts.  Overall listenable and captures the live vibe despite these imperfections.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑set outdoor Bronx gig that kicks off strong, builds into a jam‑heavy second set and closes with an emotive encore; the flow feels natural and keeps the energy high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as soaring; guitar tone noted as low in the mix but performance praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: "Phil bombs" – bass highlighted, sometimes mixed too loud but generally praised for powerful lines.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey on sabbatical (absent); Bill Kreutzmann provides steady drumming throughout.
